endorsements.quote: Clinical simulation for research is an emerging best practice method well suited for pre‐implementation testing of digital health tools, to understand the human factors, workflow changes, and unintended consequences safely and efficiently [ 1 ].
Moreover, simulation allows direct comparisons between vendor products prior to deployment.

Through this funding, the Centre for Digital Transformation of Health has partnered with rural services via the DELIVER program, supporting locally responsive pilot testing of AI scribes (including scalability and sustainment) before wider rollout.

Vendors should collaborate with research institutions and hospitals to generate the locally needed evidence, and in line with recent Government advisory, rapidly develop monitoring tools for rural health services, supporting responsible and scalable adoption.

Procurement and governance for rural AI scribe pilots should clearly assign responsibilities across the service and vendor, including what data are captured, where it is processed (e.g., local versus cloud), and how data protections and third‐party access are managed.

These include defined scope, organisational approval within a governance framework, and privacy and consent processes (including a Privacy Impact Assessment and explicit consent with an opt‐out) [ 19 ].

unlisted_practices: Consider equity as a design and evaluation dimension, informing site selection, implementation supports, and interpretation of outcomes in underserved rural populations.
Harmonise AI scribe evaluation metrics with direct input from rural health service providers and patients.

Develop shared infrastructure and protocols (consent protocols, training programs, patient communication materials, risk management, monitoring and evaluation tools) so resource-limited rural services can implement and monitor AI scribes.
Embed Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, Indigenous Data Sovereignty considerations, and culturally safe consent processes when AI scribes may capture sensitive narratives.
Test AI scribe controls such as consent prompts, pause/stop function, offline/low-bandwidth plan, and redaction during pre-implementation simulation.

Use pilot governance checklists covering data retention and deletion, data residency, encryption, sub-processor disclosure, role-based access control, offline/downtime mode, and contract clauses including change control and exit plans.
Use AI scribes to augment rather than substitute for locally based clinicians.

screen.reason: This is a commentary presenting a pragmatic strategy and key enablers for the safe implementation and deployment of ambient AI scribes in rural Australian hospitals.
